nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the forest floor limits the growth of berries, seedlings and mountain meadows beneath the canopy.

nodes.name: Peat bogs and streams
nodes.desc: The Bohemian Forest holds peat bogs and sources of rivers such as the Vltava, Otava and Uhlava, which keep soils wet.

nodes.name: Forest soil and deadwood
nodes.desc: Forest soil and rotting wood store nutrients that trees and shrubs draw on once decomposers release them.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, beetle-killed spruce and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Norway spruce
nodes.desc: Dominant conifer of the Bohemian Forest, widely planted. Spruce stands stressed by wind or drought are the main host of the spruce bark beetle.

nodes.name: European beech
nodes.desc: A broadleaf tree of the lower and middle slopes. Its nuts feed wild boar and rodents.

nodes.name: Silver birch
nodes.desc: A pioneer tree of clearings and disturbed ground, browsed by roe deer and gnawed by beavers.

nodes.name: Rowan
nodes.desc: A small tree whose berries are eaten by foxes, martens and many birds.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: Low shrub of the forest floor. Its leaves and berries feed deer, and martens take the fruit.

nodes.name: Eurasian spruce bark beetle
nodes.desc: Breeds under spruce bark and can overwhelm stressed trees in outbreaks, a major natural disturbance in Sumava.

nodes.name: European roe deer
nodes.desc: A small browsing deer that eats leaves, shoots and berries of trees and shrubs; the preferred prey of lynx where common.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: The largest deer of the forest. It grazes grasses, browses shrubs such as bilberry and is prey for wolves and lynx.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: Omnivore that roots for nuts, plants, small animals and carrion in the forest.

nodes.name: Eurasian beaver
nodes.desc: Gnaws trees and dams streams, creating wetlands. It feeds on bark and shoots of woody plants such as birch.

nodes.name: Yellow-necked mouse
nodes.desc: A forest rodent that eats seeds and small invertebrates; prey for foxes, martens and buzzards.

nodes.name: Great spotted woodpecker
nodes.desc: Splits bark to reach insect larvae, so it can help limit bark beetle numbers.

nodes.name: European pine marten
nodes.desc: Agile forest hunter that eats rodents and birds and also fruit such as rowan berries and bilberries.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Adaptable predator and scavenger that eats rodents, birds, carrion and fruit.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: Hawk that hunts rodents and other small animals over forest edges and clearings.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: Large crow that scavenges carcasses, such as those left by lynx and wolves.

nodes.name: Eurasian lynx
nodes.desc: Ambush hunter, mainly of roe deer. Wiped out in Bohemia in the 1800s, it was reintroduced to the Sumava area in the 1980s.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Pack hunter of deer and wild boar, recorded near Sumava; leaves carcasses that scavengers use.
